# Tier 1 — Frozen Files

These files must not be modified by Claude Code without the developer explicitly naming the file
in the prompt AND confirming they have spoken to the listed owner. No exceptions.

> **Note:** this is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 — paths
> below reference `overrides/app/...` (the customisation surface) rather than the upstream
> monorepo `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...` path.

## Design System (Owner: UI Designer — #design-system)

The whole `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` folder is Tier 1. Currently present:

```text
overrides/app/theme/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/motion.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts
```

**Fonts are self-hosted and served on every tier.** `overrides/app/static/fonts/` holds two
Futura Round faces — Regular 400 and Medium 500 — declared by
`overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` and mounted in both `_app-config/index.tsx` and
`.storybook/preview.tsx`. Only two faces exist because only two are used: all 22 textStyles
resolve to fontWeight 400 or 500, and `fonts.body === fonts.heading`.

There is **no environment gate** on this, and it is worth stating plainly because an earlier
revision of this section claimed there was. `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally inside
`_app-config`'s `ChakraProvider`, and `pwa-kit-dev`'s `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies
`overrides/app/static` in both the client and SSR webpack configs — so the `.woff2` are
published with every bundle and shoppers on every storefront render Futura Round.

`foundation/fonts.ts` already lists `'Futura Round'` first in both stacks, so the `@font-face`
declaration is the only thing that makes it resolve — no component, recipe or token changes.
The fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider, which is why serving the real faces matters for
design-parity review against Figma.

Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` (**Tier 2**) or, per
the co-location pattern, beside their component as `<name>.css.ts` — governed by that
component's own CODEOWNERS entry instead, not this Tier — see
[protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`
is also **Tier 2** — it composes the `.zimm-*` global class registry from the `--zimm-*`
variables defined in `foundation/zimmTokens.ts`, so it is derived styling rather than a
brand token source, but it emits CSS on every page and therefore needs a named owner.

```text

overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.ts

```

Note: `commerce-sdk-react` is consumed from `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/` —
it is not in this repo and cannot be modified here. The hooks above are the overrides surface.

## Runtime & Integration Config (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text

overrides/app/ssr.js

# Tier 2 — Protected Files

These can be modified on a feature branch but require a PR review from a developer who is not
the author before merging to develop.

> Paths reference `overrides/app/...` per this project's slim overrides layout. Override files
> keep the original Salesforce filename (kebab-case) but are TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`).

## Global Shell (Owner: Both Squads — coordinate before touching)

```text
overrides/app/components/header/
overrides/app/components/footer/
overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/
overrides/app/components/list-menu/
overrides/app/components/seo/
overrides/app/components/_app/
overrides/app/components/_app-config/
overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/
overrides/app/routes.tsx
```

`uiCopyProvider/` is mounted once inside `_app-config` and provides `useUiCopy()`'s context
value to every page on every site — the same blast radius as `_app-config` itself, so it
belongs in this tier alongside it rather than defaulting to Tier 4 by omission.

## Shared Product Components (Owner: Squad B — notify Squad A)

```text
overrides/app/components/product-tile/
overrides/app/components/product-item/
overrides/app/components/display-price/
overrides/app/components/image-gallery/
overrides/app/components/swatch-group/
overrides/app/components/recommended-products/
```

## Shared Commerce Components (Owner: Squad A — notify Squad B)

```text
overrides/app/components/order-summary/
overrides/app/components/promo-code/
overrides/app/components/pickup-or-delivery/
```

## Theme Component Styles (Owner: UI Designer — notify before changing)

```text
overrides/app/theme/components/
overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts
```

One file per Chakra component (e.g. `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`). Register new
files in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`. Foundations live alongside
in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` and are **Tier 1** — see
[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md).

A component's own recipe may instead live beside it as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g.
`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`) rather than here — see
[overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md)'s co-location pattern, introduced with the
footer decomposition. It's still registered in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`
either way. A co-located `<name>.css.ts` is **not** governed by this section's Tier 2
UI-designer gate — CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` rule routes it to
the owning squad(s) only. This folder's Tier 2 designation still applies to whatever
hasn't moved to co-location, and to genuinely cross-component shared values (e.g.
`footerShared.ts`) that a single component's file can't own.

`globalStyles.ts` is the `.zimm-*` global class registry, composed into
`theme/index.ts` as `styles.global`. It is derived from the `--zimm-*` variables in
`foundation/zimmTokens.ts` rather than defining brand values itself, so it sits at
Tier 2 — but it emits CSS on every page, so treat a change here as wider-reaching
than a single component override.

## Translations (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — notify before changing)

```text
translations/

# Zimmermann - Salesforce PWA Kit (Production)

> **STRICT RULE — TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.**
> Every file created or modified under `overrides/` **must** use `.ts` or `.tsx`.
> `.js` and `.jsx` files are not acceptable here, including theme files, stories, and config modules.
> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`.

Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com, a luxury Australian fashion brand. Must be robust and secure and SEO-friendly. See [.docs/architecture.md](.docs/architecture.md) for stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths.

Tier classifications and protected-file lists live in [.claude/rules/](.claude/rules/) — loaded automatically per session. Custom slash commands for scaffolding and review live in [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/).

## Branch Rules

**At session start, always run `git branch --show-current`.** If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — do not make any changes.

| Branch                    | Branched from          | Merges to                                                                       | Allowed?      | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `feature/*`               | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Primary working context for new work                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `fix/*`                   | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Non-urgent bug fixes. Mechanically identical to `feature/*` — naming is for commit hygiene                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `release/*`               | `develop`              | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        | ⚠️ Supervised | Plan-first + confirm-every-edit required. Code logic fixes must use a `fix/release-*` sub-branch                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch, then forward-merged to `develop` once the release ships | ✅ Yes        | Only path for code logic fixes on a release. PR targets the release branch; SIT gate runs against the PR. Treated like `feature/*` on the sub-branch itself — the "Supervised" plan-first + confirm-every-edit rules apply only to direct edits on the `release/*` branch |
| `hotfix/*`                | `main`                 | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        | ✅ Yes        | Urgent production fixes only. Tier 1 rules still apply. Must be back-merged to `develop` to prevent drift                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `develop`                 | —                      | —                                                                               | ❌ Never      | Human commits only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `main`                    | —                      | —                                                                               | ❌ Never      | Human commits only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

> **On `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branches you MUST read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) before any action.** It holds the supervised-edit rules (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, `fix/release-*` sub-branch flow) and the GitFlow back-merge rules that apply in addition to the Hard Rules below. On `feature/*` and `fix/*`, ignore it.

## Hard Rules

1. **Never operate on `develop` or `main`** branches.
2. **Never modify a Tier 1 file** without the developer explicitly naming it in the prompt and confirming owner approval — unless the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) applies. See [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md).
3. **Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`** — all design token changes go through the UI designer.
4. **Never modify `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, or `worker/main.js`.** These are absolute — the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) does not apply to them, regardless of approver status. `.github/workflows/` is Tier 1 CI/CD config and instead follows the standard Hard Rule #2 process (verified-session exception applies).
5. **Never refactor upward.** Fixing a bug in a component does not mean touching the hook or utility it calls.
6. **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.**
7. **Never add or remove packages** from `package.json` without integration team approval. When approved, always use `npm install` rather than editing `package.json` directly.
8. **Never modify test configuration files** (`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `tests/lighthouserc.js`).
9. **Never delete files** without being explicitly asked in the current prompt. You may propose deletion and let a human confirm.
10. **Never touch more than one protection tier** in a single change without stopping to confirm scope with the developer.
11. **Never assume a hook is safe to modify** because it has a simple name — check the frozenFiles list first.
12. **When requirements are unclear, ask one clarifying question at a time.** Do not proceed with assumptions and do not batch questions. Wait for the answer before asking the next question or writing any code.
13. **Never use `--dangerously-skip-permissions`** on `release/**`, `main`, or `develop`. This flag bypasses all edit confirmations and is only permitted in CI automation contexts, never in interactive developer sessions on shared or protected branches.
14. **Never reference code from a later sprint.** Check [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) before scoping any new work. If a task depends on a component, hook, or integration that belongs to a later sprint, stop and ask whether to build a placeholder or whether that sprint is already complete.
15. **Never create a git commit, push to remote, or open/close a PR** without the developer explicitly requesting it in the current prompt. Resuming from a session summary, a task list, or a "natural next step" is not an instruction to commit — wait for an explicit ask.

## Tier 1 Approval — How It's Actually Enforced

Claude Code's confirmation prompt before touching a Tier 1 file (Hard Rule #2) is a workflow
safeguard, not the security boundary — it can't be, since it only governs what Claude itself
does, not what any other tool or a direct `git push` can do. The real enforcement is server-side:

- [CODEOWNERS](../CODEOWNERS) routes every Tier 1 path to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`, a
  real GitHub org team.
- Branch protection on `develop`/`main`/`release/**` requires an approving code-owner review
  before merge — this is the actual gate, enforced natively by GitHub with no Actions
  involvement, so it can't be affected by a broken or delayed CI run.
- `.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`'s `tier1-guard` job posts a loud warning and an
  owner-contact-map on any PR touching a Tier 1 path. It is **not** a required status check —
  GitHub locked down cross-run check-run updates in Feb 2025, which made a "hard-fail until
  approved, then flip to pass on review" required check impossible to implement reliably (a
  fresh commit is needed to re-evaluate it, since a later review can't flip an earlier run's
  result). The CODEOWNERS-based review requirement above is the real, working block.

Because the actual gate lives in GitHub, not in Claude's judgement, this file does not encode
personal names or email addresses as a bypass condition — a string in a shared, version-controlled
file is not an identity check; anyone (or any other Claude session) could satisfy it by typing it.
Instead, Claude may verify the real, authenticated identity behind the current session:

- Before pausing to ask for Tier 1 confirmation, run `gh api user --jq .login`, then check
  `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members --jq '.[].login'` (or check for `admin`
  via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/collaborators/<login>/permission`). If that GitHub
  login is a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or holds repo admin, Claude may proceed
  with the edit after stating which Tier 1 file is being touched and why — no separate
  confirmation message is required, since GitHub already recognises that account as an approver.
- If the authenticated login is **not** a member/admin, Claude must still stop per Hard Rule #2:
  name the file, and require the developer to secure an approving review from
  `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` before the PR can merge. CODEOWNERS auto-requests that review
  and branch protection blocks the merge without it, regardless of what `tier1-guard` reports.
- This check only ever reduces _how many times Claude pauses to ask_. It changes nothing about
  what GitHub will actually allow to merge — that's deliberate, so a compromised or careless
  Claude session can't grant itself write access to a frozen file.

## Coding Task Workflow

Every coding task follows these four steps in order. Do not skip ahead — pause at the marked points and wait for the user.

1. **Clarify requirements.** Identify every gap, ambiguity, or contradiction in the request and the relevant `.docs/`. Confirm each one with the user before moving on — no assumptions. See Hard Rule #12: ask one question at a time.
2. **Plan.** State the files you intend to touch, _why_ each one is being touched, and any base template files that will need to be copied to `overrides/`. Then **pause** and wait for the user to confirm the plan. See the **Minimal changes** rule below.
3. **Copy first (if any).** For every base template file identified in step 2, follow the **Copy-first rule** in the Rules section. Then **pause** and let the user test and stage the override files before any functional changes.
4. **Implement.** Make the planned modifications. Remove the `console.log` markers from step 3 once the user confirms the overrides are rendering. Before committing a non-trivial code change, run a local CodeRabbit review: confirm the CLI is installed and authenticated (`coderabbit auth status`; if not authenticated, `coderabbit auth login --api-key "$CODERABBIT_API_KEY"` — see `.env.sample`), then `cr review --light --base develop` (use `main` instead on a `release/**`/`hotfix/**` branch). **The CLI is required, not optional** — if it isn't installed or authenticated, stop and have the developer install it (https://www.coderabbit.ai/cli) and run `npm run env -- init` to pull the shared key, rather than committing without a local review. The review itself is still advisory relative to the actual merge gate (the GitHub PR review remains the real gate) — use judgement on whether a flagged finding is worth fixing before the commit vs. leaving it for the PR review to catch, but the review must actually run.

**Responding to a CodeRabbit PR review.** Once CodeRabbit finishes reviewing an open PR, always leave an explicit in-thread reply for every finding, whether it's fixed or not — CodeRabbit's learning feature picks up patterns from PR conversation, so silence teaches it nothing and an explanation teaches it to stop flagging the same non-issue. A fix commit alone, with no reply posted on the thread, doesn't count. For a finding that gets fixed, a short in-thread reply confirming the fix (referencing the commit is fine) is enough. For a finding that is *not* being fixed because it conflicts with this repo's own rules/docs/architecture (e.g. a Tier 1 exception that was actually followed correctly, an intentional design tradeoff already recorded in `.docs/`) — reply in-thread explaining the specific rule or doc that justifies not changing it, so CodeRabbit's learning has the context to recognise the same pattern next time instead of re-flagging it. Never silently dismiss a finding without a reply.

## When to Stop and Ask a Human

| Trigger                                                                      | Action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Task requires a Tier 1 file                                                  | Check the authenticated `gh` identity against `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`/admin (see [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced)). If verified, name the file and proceed. Otherwise stop and require named owner approval. |

Requires a team RFC.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Integration team must approve.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Current branch is `develop` or `main`                                        | Stop immediately. No changes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

Integration team sign-off required.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

Confirm scope with the developer before continuing.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Requirement is missing, ambiguous, contradictory, or unconfirmed in `.docs/` | Stop. Flag, propose, wait for approval (see Requirements section).                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Multi-site & Routing

The SFCC sites are hard routing and config boundaries — **never bleed config across sites.** Never assume a storefront's routing, URL prefix, checkout ownership, or consent defaults without checking [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md).

## Accessibility

## Rules

*Day-to-day code-writing conventions live in `.claude/rules/` and load automatically:
[conventions.md](.claude/rules/conventions.md) (cross-cutting: naming, imports, DRY, security),
[typescript.md](.claude/rules/typescript.md) (TS idioms), [css.md](.claude/rules/css.md)
(Chakra tokens, `.scss`), and [components.md](.claude/rules/components.md)
(component/hook/utility structure, Storybook categorisation, composition). The rules below
are project-specific behaviours and security guardrails that don't fit there.*

- **No mocking:** All data must come from the live Commerce Cloud API via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks. No MSW or hardcoded fixtures in production paths.

#!/bin/bash
# Pre-commit hook:
#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
#
# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
  # nvm (most common on macOS)
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

  # fnm
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi

  # volta
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
  fi

  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)

registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)

if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
  git add .claude/registry/
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
    || true)

  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
    if ! node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null; then
      echo ""
      echo "  ❌  sync:ai-rules:fix failed — derived AI config files may be stale or partially"
      echo "      written. Fix the error above, then re-stage and commit again."
      echo ""
      exit 1
    fi
    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
#     automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'

  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
  fi

  echo ""
  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
  echo ""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen
#    When any experiences/*.tsx file is staged, regenerate definitions.ts
#    and stage it automatically. Blocks the commit on codegen failure.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

experiences_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E 'overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/.*\.tsx$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$experiences_staged" ]; then
  echo "Studio Experiences component staged — regenerating definitions.ts..."

  REAL_EXPERIENCES="overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences"
  tmp_exp=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_exp"' EXIT

  # Populate temp dir with the staged version of each .tsx.
  # Files that are not staged are copied from the working tree so the generator
  # sees a complete set. definitions.ts is excluded — it is the output target.
  for f in "$REAL_EXPERIENCES"/*.tsx; do
    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    name=$(basename "$f")
    [[ "$name" == "definitions.ts" ]] && continue
    if echo "$experiences_staged" | grep -qF "$f"; then
      git show ":0:$f" > "$tmp_exp/$name"
    else
      cp "$f" "$tmp_exp/$name"
    fi
  done

  if ! CF_EXPERIENCES_DIR="$tmp_exp" node scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Contentful codegen failed. Fix the errors above and try again."
    exit 1
  fi

  cp "$tmp_exp/definitions.ts" "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
  git add "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
  echo "  ✓  definitions.ts updated and staged."
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Derived configuration file guard
#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

blocked_files=()

# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)

while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

  # Only check files in derived locations
  case "$file" in
    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac

  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue

  # Extract all source paths from the synced-from comment
  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2, ...] — ... -->
  synced_sources=$(echo "$synced_line" \
    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//')

  [[ -z "$synced_sources" ]] && continue

  # If ANY source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
  # update — the developer edited a .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
  # Skip it.
  staged_names=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
  any_source_staged=false
  while IFS= read -r src; do
    src=$(echo "$src" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
    [[ -z "$src" ]] && continue
    if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qxF -- "$src"; then
      any_source_staged=true
      break
    fi
  done <<< "$(echo "$synced_sources" | tr ',' '\n')"
  if $any_source_staged; then
    continue
  fi

  # Fall back to the same AI-sources trigger condition step 1b uses to decide
  # whether to regenerate this file in the first place. A derived file's own
  # synced-from header may not yet list every source that legitimately feeds
  # it (e.g. a skill file added after the header was last written) — if step
  # 1b would have regenerated this file because a .claude/rules/*.md or
  # .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md file is staged, that is also a legitimate sync,
  # not a direct edit.
  if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qE '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$'; then
    continue
  fi

  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
  blocked_files+=("$file")

done <<< "$modified_staged"

if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
  echo ""
  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
    echo "       $bf"
  done
  echo ""
  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
  echo ""
  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
  echo ""
  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
  secret_violations=()

  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a JWT
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value matches a known provider secret format)")
      continue
    fi

  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)

  if [ "${#secret_violations[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
    echo ""
    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
      echo "    $v"
    done
    echo ""
    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
    echo ""
    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
fi

exit 0

    if echo "$experiences_staged" | grep -qF "$f"; then
      git show ":0:$f" > "$tmp_exp/$name"
    else
      cp "$f" "$tmp_exp/$name"
    fi
  done

  if ! CF_EXPERIENCES_DIR="$tmp_exp" node scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Contentful codegen failed. Fix the errors above and try again."
    exit 1
  fi

  cp "$tmp_exp/definitions.ts" "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
  git add "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
  echo "  ✓  definitions.ts updated and staged."
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Derived configuration file guard
#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

blocked_files=()

# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)

while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

  # Only check files in derived locations
  case "$file" in
    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac

  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue

  # Extract all source paths from the synced-from comment
  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2, ...] — ... -->
  synced_sources=$(echo "$synced_line" \
    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//')

  [[ -z "$synced_sources" ]] && continue

  # If ANY source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
  # update — the developer edited a .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
  # Skip it.
  staged_names=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
  any_source_staged=false
  while IFS= read -r src; do
    src=$(echo "$src" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
    [[ -z "$src" ]] && continue
    if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qxF -- "$src"; then
      any_source_staged=true
      break
    fi
  done <<< "$(echo "$synced_sources" | tr ',' '\n')"
  if $any_source_staged; then
    continue
  fi

  # Fall back to the same AI-sources trigger condition step 1b uses to decide
  # whether to regenerate this file in the first place. A derived file's own
  # synced-from header may not yet list every source that legitimately feeds
  # it (e.g. a skill file added after the header was last written) — if step
  # 1b would have regenerated this file because a .claude/rules/*.md or
  # .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md file is staged, that is also a legitimate sync,
  # not a direct edit.
  if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qE '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$'; then
    continue
  fi

  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
  blocked_files+=("$file")

done <<< "$modified_staged"

if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
  echo ""
  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
    echo "       $bf"
  done
  echo ""
  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
  echo ""
  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
  echo ""
  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.

#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
  secret_violations=()

  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a JWT
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
      continue
    fi

    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
    echo ""

      echo "    $v"
    done
    echo ""
    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
    echo ""
    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
fi

name: Protected File Guard

# Server-side enforcement of the tier/squad model. The client-side
# .claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh is non-blocking — this workflow is the
# authoritative gate at PR time.

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - develop
      - main
      - 'release/**'
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 1 — Warning (non-blocking): Tier 1 files touched.
  # NOT a required status check (see AGENTS.md > Tier 1 Approval for why).
  # The actual hard block is CODEOWNERS + require_code_owner_reviews on
  # branch protection, enforced natively by GitHub with no Actions
  # involvement. This job exists to post the loud, informative warning and
  # owner-contact-map — useful context, not the gate itself.
  #
  # History: this used to be a required check with a second job
  # (tier1-guard-recheck) that re-evaluated it on every review submission
  # via the Checks API, so it could flip from fail to pass without a new
  # commit. That approach stopped working once GitHub locked down check-run
  # updates to same-run-only in Feb 2025 (see
  # https://github.blog/changelog/2025-02-12-notice-of-upcoming-deprecations-and-breaking-changes-for-github-actions/#changes-to-check-run-status-modification) —
  # a different workflow run can no longer flip another run's check
  # conclusion. Since a single pull_request-triggered run can't wait around
  # for a future review, and re-running the whole job on review events just
  # creates a second, stale-vs-fresh check-run record under the same name
  # (which GitHub does NOT treat the newer one as superseding for
  # merge-blocking purposes), there's no way to make this job itself both
  # required and reliably self-updating. CODEOWNERS already does this
  # correctly and natively, so that's the real gate.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  tier1-guard:
    name: "🔴 Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

      - name: Get changed files
        id: changed
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          base_sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          files_yaml: |
            tier1:
              # Design tokens — owner: UI Designer
              - 'overrides/app/theme/foundation/**'
              - 'overrides/app/theme/index.ts'
              # Commerce SDK hooks (overrides surface) — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-token.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.*'
              # Runtime & integration config — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'config/**'
              - 'overrides/app/ssr.*'
              - 'worker/main.*'
              - 'mobify.config.js'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'package-lock.json'
              # Test & tooling config — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'vitest.config.*'
              - 'playwright.config.*'
